notes:
ROBOTS: https://www.connox.com/robots.txt fetched FIRST, before any other request on the host (saved at work/w105_108/connox_robots.txt, HTTP 200, 261 bytes) and re-verified by me rather than taken from the previous worker's dump. It is a single 'User-agent: *' group with five Disallows - /customer-area.html, /watch-list.html, /customer-area/, /design-newsletter-registered.html, /orly.php - plus two Sitemap lines. NO Claude agent is named: no ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai or Claude-Web group, and no Content-Signal line. None of the five disallowed paths is anywhere near the category tree. No Crawl-delay is declared, so probe.py's 2 s per-host gap was used unchanged. SECOND HOST: the PLP renders from api.connox.io, a different host, so per the per-host rule I fetched https://api.connox.io/robots.txt separately BEFORE using it - it returns HTTP 404, i.e. no robots file and therefore no directive of any kind, named or generic. cdn.connox.com and cdn.connox.de were deliberately NOT used: both JS bundles I read are also served from www.connox.com and I took them from there so no third host was touched. ACCESS: plain HTTP 200 on every page via probe.fetch(); no bot wall, no interstitial, no 403. The storefront is served in English with c_ActiveCountry = 'DE' and body data-channel = '100005', i.e. this is the German channel of connox.com. The manifest site for SR 108 is https://www.connox.com/ and Furniture.xlsx already recorded all 50 of its Connox rows on connox.com English URLs (verified by dumping every connox key in the exclusion index), so the URL form used here is consistent with the prior pass. TREE: taken from the site's own taxonomy, not guessed. Connox has two parallel structures and I used the product one. (1) /bathroom.html is category type 'Raum' (room) under Inspiration > Rooms - an editorial room hub whose four children are type 'Seite' with zero products; it is NOT the product tree. (2) The product tree is Categories > Home Accessories > Bathroom Decor at https://www.connox.com/categories/accessories/bathroom-accessories.html (categoryId 102051, type 'Produktkategorie'). Its children came from that page's own 'All categories in Bathroom Decor' block (28 links, 27 unique), cross-checked against the rendered mega-menu on the home page, which lists the same set. Every page reports its own identity in three independent places that I read on every fetch: body id='C', the dataLayer push ('CategoryId', 'CategoryTypeId', 'CategoryTypeName'), and the rendered breadcrumb + BreadcrumbList ld+json. HIDDEN-CHILD CHECK (this is what a mega-menu 'Mehr' truncation would hide): I downloaded all eight sitemap files declared in robots.txt (13,587 URLs, 13,087 of them under /categories/) and derived the child set independently from URL structure - every product under a Bathroom Decor subcategory lives at /categories/accessories/bathroom-accessories//.html, so the distinct second-level segments ARE the child set. That produced 20 segments against the nav's 21 in-path children. The six segments the nav did not show (bathroom-attachments, bathroom-equipment, care-wellness, hand-creams, soap-dishes, soap-dispensers) were each fetched and every one is a legacy path alias that resolves to a category I already had: bathroom-attachments.html and care-wellness.html -> C102051 Bathroom Decor, bathroom-equipment.html -> C111060 the room hub, soap-dishes.html -> C186118 (canonical is the bathroom-attachments/soap-dishes.html form the nav uses, which is what rows[] records), soap-dispensers.html -> C125172, hand-creams.html 404s. So the child set is closed - there is no truncated branch. QTY: the PLP is fully client-rendered (
), so there is no rendered total in the HTML and no pagination markup. I therefore used the storefront's OWN product API - the one the PLP itself renders from, established by reading the site's React bundle https://www.connox.com/script/cnxwp.124.min.js: fetchProductList -> Items.getItems -> GET `/shop/${shopId}/items?${query}` against base https://api.connox.io/v1, where shopId = document.body.dataset.channel (100005 on these pages) and the query builder seeds queryParams with view:'search' and adds categoryId, limit, offset, currencyCode; the response fields it consumes are itemContent and totalSearchHits. The exact request form used here is https://api.connox.io/v1/shop/100005/items?view=search&limit=&offset=¤cyCode=EUR&categoryId=, and the categoryId is always the one the PLP itself declares in its own body id / dataLayer. No parameter was invented. VERIFICATION: (a) EQUIVALENCE PROVED BY EXHAUSTIVE ENUMERATION on four categories of deliberately different size - Washing accessories (191688), Shower squeegee (183850), Toothbrush mug (183844) and Soap dispenser (125172). Paging offset=0,100,200... to exhaustion and counting itemIds gave total / fetched / unique = 4/4/4, 29/29/29, 106/106/106 and 119/119/119. totalSearchHits therefore equals the real number of distinct products on the grid, on small, medium and multi-page nodes alike, and is not a filtered or capped figure. (b) H1 and breadcrumb were checked on EVERY node and match the node asked for: all nine recorded leaves render breadcrumb 'Categories > Home Accessories > Bathroom Decor' with an H1 equal to the nav label (Bath shelves & Shower shelves, Cosmetic tissue boxes, Shower squeegee, Soap dishes, Soap dispenser, Toilet brushes, Toilet roll holder, Toothbrush mug, Towel rail) and CategoryTypeName 'Produktunterkategorie'. Nodes whose breadcrumb showed a different parent (Home Textiles, Home Decor, Household) were routed out on that evidence, not on their name. (c) Counts discriminate strongly and are nowhere a site-wide constant: 4, 7, 9, 17, 21, 22, 29, 29, 35, 39, 48, 49, 50, 55, 56, 67, 98, 99, 101, 106, 113, 119, 137, 154, 280, 351, 418. (d) Ambiguous nodes were resolved by reading their actual product titles through the same API rather than by keyword: 'Washing accessories' turned out to be four Steamery laundry-detergent items, 'Lint brushes & Lint shaver' seven Steamery garment-care tools, 'Body care' Meraki shampoo and body wash - all three routed out; 'Cosmetic tissue boxes' (Nichba wall paper dispenser, Zone Denmark Ume handkerchief boxes, Alessi Birillo tissue box) and 'Bath shelves & Shower shelves' (Umbra Cubiko shower trays, Zone Denmark Ume jars, Mette Ditmer marble cube) are genuine bathroom accessories and are recorded. ASSORTMENT - EXPLICIT NEGATIVE FINDING: Connox is a design-homeware retailer and sells NO sanitaryware. I searched the full 13,587-URL sitemap for washbasin, wash-basin, bathtub, bath-tub, faucet, sanitary, shower-head, toilet-seat and waschbecken: the only hits anywhere on the site are two product pages whose names merely contain the words (Radius Design Puro towel holder for a washbasin; Umbra Aquala bathtub shelf). There is no baths, toilets, basins, taps, showers or enclosures node, so rules 4-8 have no nodes here, and rule 9 (bathroom furniture / vanity units) has none either - the site's only 'Bathroom furniture' URL is an empty editorial 'Seite'. Rule 10 (mirrors) was actively checked and Connox's mirror categories are all filed under Home Decor / Entryway Furniture with no bathroom mirror node; they are in review[] routed to Decor rather than skipped. These absences are facts about the assortment, established by search, not gaps in the walk. DEDUP: already_extracted() was run on all 29 candidate URLs (the nine recorded leaves, the hub, and every routed-out or withheld node). ZERO hits - the Furniture pass took 50 Connox URLs but all of them are furniture, outdoor and kids nodes and none is in the bathroom branch. So no OPTION 1 exclusion applies to this company and all nine leaves are genuinely unextracted. EXCLUDED: 'Bathroom Decor' (102051) is a grouping row with blank qty and blank link (rule 38); its own totalSearchHits is 13 and all 13 items belong to four type-'Produkt' single-product landing nodes, which confirms it has no grid of its own worth recording and is not a leaf. /bathroom.html (418) is withheld as a room-level roll-up that spans the recorded leaves (roll-up rule + rule 24). The three 'Produkt' landing pages in the hub's child list are not categories (rule 27). The four /bathroom/* editorial pages are EMPTY NODES (0 products each) and named in review[]. Five textile nodes (Bath towels 101, Bathrobes 39, Bath mats 49, Shower Curtains 35, Towels 280) route to Textile; Scented candles 99 and the two mirror nodes (351, 154) route to Decor; Body care 21, Hand creams 17, Soaps 29, Toiletry bags 48, Washing accessories 4, Lint brushes 7, Steam straightener 9, Trash cans 137, Laundry baskets 113 and Hot-water bottles 4 are not Bathroom by primary product type or by the site's own hierarchy. All are in review[] with qty and URL so nothing is silently skipped.
